t: #2550 Count Collisions of Monkeys on a Polygon
o: Each monkey independently picks clockwise or counter-clockwise: 2^n total assignments. The only collision-free movements are all-clockwise and all-counter-clockwise (any mixed assignment makes two adjacent monkeys move toward each other or onto the same vertex). So the answer is 2^n - 2 modulo 1e9+7. Check: n=3 gives 8-2=6, n=4 gives 16-2=14. Since n can be 1e9, we need fast modular exponentiation.
k: Exactly two movement patterns avoid collisions: everyone rotates the same direction.
Answer = (2^n - 2) mod 1e9+7, computed with binary exponentiation in O(log n).

a.i: Compute pow(2, n, MOD) via repeated squaring, subtract 2, adjust modulo.
s: Subtract 2 and add MOD if negative.

w: The whole problem reduces to proving the complement count is 2. JavaScript needs BigInt because intermediate squares exceed 2^53. Follow-up: what if monkeys could also stay put (answer becomes 3^n - 2)?
